# Nivutakathā (Kv 13.5)

**ID:** Kv 13.5
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Nivutakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul20.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nivutakathā* (Kv 13.5) is a debate situated in the thirteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The text examines whether an individual who is obstructed or hindered (*nivuta*) can abandon the hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*) [Bareau 1955]. In his study of early Buddhist sectarian doctrines, André Bareau notes the opposing propositions debated on this theme: on the one side, the proposition that someone who is subject to hindrances does not abandon them—drawing analogies with the premise that an impassioned person (*ratta*) does not abandon passion (*rāga*), or an angry person hatred (*dosa*)—and on the other, the thesis that one who is enveloped and obstructed by hindrances can abandon them through the process of purification that must be realized [Bareau 1955].

  It also notes a low-scoring cross-language match with the Tibetan *Āgamakṣudrakavyākhyāna* (D 4115) [DharmaNexus].
